accommodations.name: The Quigley Residence
accommodations.description: Exclusively dedicated to postgraduate and medical students, The Quigley Residence is located on the North Campus adjacent to the Medical School and Irish World Academy. It offers a quieter, mature environment conducive to study. The residence shares a reception with Cappavilla Village and features modern apartments in an attractive landscaped setting.
amenities: Full access to UL Sport gym & pool
pros: Exclusively for postgraduate students, ensuring a quiet study environment
Located on-campus, close to Health Sciences and Medical School
All rooms are ensuite with modern facilities
cons: More expensive than some other on-campus options
Limited parking availability
Shared reception with Cappavilla Village (can be busy)

accommodations.name: Drominbeg Square (Rhebogue Student Village)
accommodations.description: UL's newest off-campus village, located in the Rhebogue area approximately 3km from the main campus. Specifically catering to postgraduate students on 51-week contracts, it offers a mix of ensuite and non-ensuite rooms in 3, 4, and 6-bedroom houses. It is connected to the university via the Canal Bank river path, suitable for cycling or walking.
amenities: Full access to UL Sport gym & pool
pros: 51-week contract option ideal for Masters/PhD students
Quiet residential location away from the bustle of undergrad nightlife
Newer facilities with in-house laundry
cons: Located 3km from campus (further than other villages)
Requires commuting (bike/bus/walk)
Limited parking available

accommodations.name: Cappavilla Village
accommodations.description: Located on the North Campus at the highest point, offering stunning views of the River Shannon and surrounding counties. It is an apartment-style residence popular with health science and music students due to its proximity to those buildings. While mixed, it often houses many postgraduates in specific blocks.
amenities: Full access to UL Sport gym & pool
pros: All bedrooms have private ensuite bathrooms
Scenic views and quiet atmosphere on North Campus
Close to Irish World Academy and Health Sciences building
cons: 15-20 minute walk to the main campus/library via the Living Bridge
Can feel isolated from the main social hubs
Electric heating can be expensive if usage limits exceeded (though utilities generally included)

accommodations.name: Thomond Village
accommodations.description: Situated on the North Campus, linked to the south bank by the spectacular Living Bridge. It offers spectacular views of the River Shannon. The village consists of apartment-style accommodation and shares a reception and study hub. It is a large village that houses a mix of students but has dedicated postgraduate apartments.
amenities: Full access to UL Sport gym & pool
pros: Modern apartment style with ensuite rooms
Beautiful riverside location and views
Access to a dedicated study hub
cons: Walking distance to main campus classes (10-15 mins)
Windy crossing the bridge in winter
Large village can be noisy depending on block allocation

accommodations.name: Dromroe Village
accommodations.description: An attractive apartment-style complex bordering the millstream and overlooking the Shannon River. It is located very centrally on the main campus, close to the main teaching buildings and the University Concert Hall. It has a village feel with an on-site pizza place and shop.
amenities: Full access to UL Sport gym & pool
pros: Central on-campus location, very short walk to classes
Ensuite bathrooms in all rooms
Excellent on-site facilities (shop, food, seminar rooms)
cons: Can be noisy due to central location and on-site retail
Parking is limited and not guaranteed
High demand makes it difficult to secure a room

accommodations.name: Troy Village
accommodations.description: Located in the Groody area of Castletroy, approximately a 15-minute walk from the main UL campus. Managed by UL Campus Life Services, it offers a secure, gated community feel. It is a popular choice for students who want a slightly cheaper option while remaining under university management.
amenities: Full access to UL Sport gym & pool
pros: More affordable than on-campus ensuite villages
Shops and supermarkets (Groody Centre) nearby
Quiet, gated community safe for residents
cons: 15-20 minute walk to campus (not immediate access)
Some rooms have shared bathrooms (Standard options)
Limited parking availability

accommodations.name: Groody Village (UL Managed)
accommodations.description: Located in the Groody area, close to Troy Village and about 15 minutes walk from campus. UL Campus Life Services manages specific blocks within this development. It offers modern apartment living with a mix of ensuite and standard rooms. Residents here have access to the same support network as other UL managed villages.
amenities: Full access to UL Sport gym & pool
pros: Close to supermarkets and local amenities
Includes UL Sport membership and campus support
Modern fittings with in-unit laundry
cons: 15-minute walk to campus
Standard rooms share bathrooms
Not directly on the main campus shuttle route (though close)

accommodations.name: Groody Student Park (Private)
accommodations.description: A privately managed student accommodation complex located in the Castletroy area, adjacent to the UL-managed Groody Village. It is very popular with postgraduates and international students. The complex features 3-bedroom apartments and 6-bedroom duplexes within a secure gated community.
pros: Private management allows for different booking flexibility
Spacious living areas with double beds in many rooms
Walking distance to ALDI, SuperValu, and cinema
cons: Utilities often charged separately or as a prepaid allowance
Booking process is separate from the central UL lottery
15-20 minute walk to UL main building

accommodations.name: Brookfield Hall
accommodations.description: A purpose-built private student complex located on the Groody Road. It is well-regarded for its high-quality facilities and includes a shuttle bus service to UL. It offers spacious apartments with all ensuite bedrooms and double beds, making it a premium choice for postgraduates.
pros: Free shuttle bus service is a major convenience
All rooms are ensuite with double bed options
Dedicated block often available for postgraduates
cons: Slightly more expensive than some other off-campus options
Strict cancellation policies
High demand leads to early sell-out

accommodations.name: Plassey Village
accommodations.description: One of the original on-campus villages, consisting of terraced houses arranged around courtyards. While typically popular with first-year undergraduates due to its social atmosphere, it offers an affordable on-campus option. Accommodations are generally 8-bedroom houses with shared bathrooms.
amenities: Full access to UL Sport gym & pool
pros: Most affordable on-campus option
Located very close to the main university entrance and bus stops
Strong community feel
cons: Predominantly undergraduate/fresher population (can be noisy)
Shared bathrooms (no ensuite)
Older housing stock compared to Cappavilla/Thomond

accommodations.name: Kilmurry Village
accommodations.description: Located near the UL Sport Arena, this village consists of terraced houses in a landscaped setting. It is ideal for sports enthusiasts. Like Plassey, it has a strong undergraduate presence but offers 6 and 8-bedroom houses. It is close to the running track and swimming pool.
pros: Immediate access to world-class sports facilities
Good balance of cost and location
Spacious kitchen/living areas
cons: Shared bathrooms (no ensuite)
Can be noisy with undergraduate students
Slightly further from main reception than Plassey

accommodations.name: Parkview Hall
accommodations.description: A purpose-built student apartment complex located on the Dublin Road, roughly a 25-30 minute walk from the university. It offers budget-friendly accommodation in 3-bedroom apartments. It is a quieter option often chosen by students who miss out on closer villages or want to save money.
pros: More affordable monthly rent compared to villages
Near local bus stops for city and university access
Quieter than the main student hubs
cons: Longer walk to campus (25-30 mins)
Electricity is often pre-pay (Pinergy) and extra
Facilities are more basic than luxury student builds
